Quick technical update — triage findings so far:
- Root cause: bursty multi-tenant job saturated a subset of GPU hosts; autoscaler did not trigger fast enough due to a conservative cool-down.
- Symptoms: KV cache pressure leading to cache thrashing; larger sequences amplified kernel compute time -> higher tail latency.
- Short-term mitigations (in flight):
  * Bump emergency pool by 4 nodes and route prod-1 (ETA 18 min)
  * Apply temporary tenant-level concurrency cap of 40% for non-reserved tenants in the pool (ETA 8 min)
  * Flip to quantized model variant for prod-1 to shave ~15% CPU/GPU time for high-throughput calls (ETA 22 min, will validate quality quickly)

Attachments: pool-heatmap-0909.png (visual of host saturation).

If emergency nodes come up and we route traffic, we should see throughput recover to >= committed baseline within ~20–30 minutes. If not, we'll fall back to routing to a different region (longer latency) while we keep the customer updated.

— Rishi
